Dosage form(s): Acceptable dosage forms for all NHPs
Cream; Emulsion; Foam; Gel; Liquid; Lotion; Ointment; Paste; Pressed powder; Salve; Solution; Suspension; Topical liquid
Acceptable dosage forms for NHPs not containing nano titanium dioxide or nano zinc oxide
Aerosol; Aerosol, spray; Loose powder; Spray; Spray (bag-on-valve)
Acceptable dosage forms for NPDs
Aerosol; Aerosol, spray; Cream; Emulsion; Foam; Gel; Lotion; Ointment; Paste; Powder; Salve; Solution; Spray; Spray (bag-on-valve); Stick; Suspension

Use(s) or Purpose(s): All products (mandatory)
Sun Protection Factor "X"/SPF "X" *
All products (optional)
Helps prevent sunburn
Sunscreen
Sunburn protectant
Helps protect from sunburn
Products with a critical wavelength of ≥ 370 nm ** and with medicinal ingredient(s) that provide UVA and UVB protection (optional)
Broad spectrum
Products with a critical wavelength of ≥ 370 nm ** , with medicinal ingredient(s) that provide UVA and UVB protection, and SPF ≥ 15 (optional)
Filters/Screens UVA/UVB rays
Absorbs throughout the UVA/UVB spectrum to provide sunburn protection
UVA/UVB protection
Products that are water resistant *** (optional)
Water/Sweat Resistant [40 minutes/80 minutes]
Products with a critical wavelength of ≥ 370 nm, with medicinal ingredient(s) that provide UVA and UVB protection, and SPF ≥ 15 (optional)
If used as directed with other sun protection measures [see Directions (for Use)], decreases the risk of skin cancer and early skin aging caused by the sun.
Note: For NPDs, to ensure consistency in the labelling requirements for primary sunscreens, products making any of the above claims are eligible for the labelling flexibilities set out in section 2.6 of the Labelling
requirements for non-prescription drugs guidance document except for the warning statement regarding the risk of rashes, as mentioned in the Risk information section below.

Use(s) or Purpose(s): * As determined using a standardized and reproducible method, such as the ones referenced in the US FDA 2021 M020 monograph, ISO 24444, ISO 23675 and ISO 23698. The SPF value must be ≥ 2 and values greater than 50 are to be declared as SPF 50+.
** As determined using a standardized and reproducible method, such as the ones referenced in the US FDA 2021 M020 monograph, ISO 24443, ISO 23698 and Colipa 2011.
*** As determined using a standardized and reproducible method, such as the ones referenced in the US FDA 2021 M020 monograph and Colipa 2005. When the Colipa methodology is used, the labelled SPF value must be the SPF value of the final product formulation determined following immersion (Antoniou et al. 2008).
Unacceptable use(s) or purpose(s)
See Appendix 1 .
Notes
PA rating (Protection grade of UVA)
The PA rating system was developed in Japan and is currently used by most Asian countries.
This system addresses UVA protection based on the Persistent Pigment Darkening method (e.g., ISO 24442).
For NPD ingredients, data must be provided to NNHPD through the labelling only submission pathway to support any additional information regarding the PA rating.

Use(s) or Purpose(s): For NHP products containing zinc oxide or a combination of zinc oxide and titanium dioxide, the PA rating is acceptable as additional information on the label, as long as it is truthful and not misleading. Valid data using a standardized and reproducible method must be available upon request. This does not apply to titanium dioxide alone which is less effective at blocking long-wave UVA (UVA I) rays.
Subpopulation(s): Infants 6 to 12 months, Children 1 to 11 years, Adolescents 12 to 17 years, Adults 18 years and older.

Direction(s) for use: All products excluding sprays and aerosols
Apply liberally/generously (and evenly) 15 minutes before sun exposure
Reapply at least every 2 hours
Sun Protection Measures: Spending time in the sun increases your risk of skin cancer and early skin aging. To decrease this risk, regularly use a sunscreen with a Broad Spectrum SPF value of 15 or higher and other sun protection measures including:
limit time in the sun, especially from 10 a.m. – 2 p.m./11 a.m. – 3 p.m. * /10 a.m. – 3 p.m.; and
wear long-sleeved shirts, pants, hats, and sunglasses
* Note : As per Health Canada public health communication on sunscreens , it should be noted that in Canada, the sun's UV rays are strongest between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.
Sprays and aerosols
Spray liberally/generously and spread evenly by hand 15 minutes before sun exposure
Hold container 4 to 6 inches/10 to 15 centimetres from the skin to apply
Do not spray directly onto face. Spray on hands then apply to face
Do not apply in windy conditions
Use in a well-ventilated area
Avoid inhaling or exposing others to spray
Reapply at least every 2 hours

Direction(s) for use: Sun Protection Measures: Spending time in the sun increases your risk of skin cancer and early skin aging. To decrease this risk, regularly use a sunscreen with a Broad Spectrum SPF value of 15 or higher and other sun protection measures including:
limit time in the sun, especially from 10 a.m. – 2 p.m./11 a.m. – 3 p.m. * /10 a.m. – 3 p.m.; and
wear long-sleeved shirts, pants, hats, and sunglasses.
* See the note listed in the previous section.
All products (optional)
Test on a small area of skin before first use. If irritation occurs (within 24 hours), use a different product
Products that are non-water resistant
Use a water resistant sunscreen if swimming or sweating.
Products that are water resistant
Reapply after 40/80 minutes of swimming or sweating.
Reapply immediately after towel drying.
Products that are applied to the lips
Reapply after eating or drinking

Caution(s) and warning(s): All products
For external use only
When using this product avoid contact with eyes. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water (US FDA 2021).
Stop use and ask a health care practitioner/health care provider/health care professional/doctor/physician if rash occurs **** (US FDA 2021).
Keep out of reach of children. If swallowed, call a poison control centre or get medical help right away
**** For NPDs, this warning statement must appear on the outer label of all primary sunscreen products, and is ineligible for Level 4 Graduated and Labelling for Low-Risk Non-prescription Drugs (Category I) flexibilities as described in the Guidance Document: Labelling Requirements for Non-prescription Drugs .
Products with a critical wavelength of < 370 nm or with SPF value of < 15
Other warnings Skin Cancer/Skin Aging Alert: Spending time in the sun increases your risk of skin cancer and
early skin aging. This product has been
shown only to help prevent sunburn, not skin cancer or early skin aging (US FDA 2021).

Contraindication(s): All products
Do not use on broken skin (US FDA 2021).
